meta.purpose: Research corpus for the Librarian agent (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Phase 8, agent 2). Task B assumes 'a research literature corpus'; this is a small, honest one.
meta.sources: Paper abstracts (arXiv/SSRN), published anomaly lists in Harvey-Liu-Zhu (2016) and Hou-Xue-Zhang (2020), Kakushadze (2016) '101 Formulaic Alphas', and standard textbook factor descriptions. Abstracts and factor descriptions ONLY - no paywalled full text, no login-walled scraping.
meta.tradeable_with_our_data: true iff the anomaly can be built from daily OHLCV, VWAP, number-of-trades, delivery percentage (>=2019-09-30), a trailing-turnover size proxy, and a static sector label. false = needs fundamentals / earnings / analyst / short-interest / options / news data we do not have.

anomalies.name: price momentum (12-1)
anomalies.mechanism: investors underreact to gradual information, so past 3-12 month relative winners keep outperforming past losers
anomalies.counterparty: attention-constrained investors and the disposition effect (holding losers, selling winners too early)
anomalies.known_decay: persistent globally but weaker and more crash-prone since ~2009; severe drawdowns after market rebounds

anomalies.name: short-term reversal (1 month)
anomalies.mechanism: liquidity provision and price pressure: last month's biggest movers overshoot and partly revert as inventory clears
anomalies.counterparty: liquidity demanders who trade impatiently; market makers earn the reversal as compensation
anomalies.known_decay: strong in illiquid names, largely arbitraged in large caps; concentrated in the first few days

anomalies.name: 52-week high proximity
anomalies.mechanism: the 52-week high is an anchor; investors underreact to good news when price nears the high, so nearness predicts continuation
anomalies.counterparty: anchoring-biased investors reluctant to bid a stock above its salient prior high
anomalies.known_decay: still present; overlaps mechanically with momentum

anomalies.name: idiosyncratic volatility puzzle
anomalies.mechanism: high-idiosyncratic-vol stocks earn LOW subsequent returns - overpricing by lottery-seeking, undervaluation-correction constrained by limits to arbitrage
anomalies.counterparty: retail investors with a preference for volatile, skewed payoffs
anomalies.known_decay: robust but partly explained by MAX and short-term reversal; sensitive to how vol is measured

anomalies.name: MAX lottery effect
anomalies.mechanism: stocks with extreme recent single-day gains are overbought by lottery-preferring investors and underperform
anomalies.counterparty: retail investors chasing salient recent jackpots
anomalies.known_decay: persistent; strongest in small, retail-held names

anomalies.name: betting against beta / low-beta
anomalies.mechanism: leverage-constrained investors overweight high-beta stocks, bidding their prices up and future returns down; low-beta earns a premium per unit risk
anomalies.counterparty: leverage-constrained funds and investors who reach for return via beta instead of borrowing
anomalies.known_decay: still present; implementation-sensitive (needs shorting high-beta)

anomalies.name: Amihud illiquidity premium
anomalies.mechanism: less liquid stocks (higher price impact per rupee traded) must offer higher expected returns to compensate holders
anomalies.counterparty: investors who need immediacy and pay the impact; long-horizon holders harvest the premium
anomalies.known_decay: compressed as trading costs fell; still visible in small caps and EM

anomalies.name: share turnover / trading activity
anomalies.mechanism: high turnover proxies for overvaluation and disagreement; high-turnover stocks subsequently underperform
anomalies.counterparty: disagreeing, overconfident traders who churn positions
anomalies.known_decay: still present; entangled with size and liquidity

anomalies.name: high-volume return premium
anomalies.mechanism: a spike in trading volume raises a stock's visibility and investor base, pushing price up over the following weeks (shift in recognition)
anomalies.counterparty: investors who only buy stocks that have recently caught their attention
anomalies.known_decay: documented in US; weaker in liquid mega caps

anomalies.name: Corwin-Schultz high-low spread
anomalies.mechanism: the daily high-low range embeds the effective bid-ask spread; a wider implied spread signals higher illiquidity and a return premium
anomalies.counterparty: immediacy demanders paying the spread
anomalies.known_decay: a spread estimator more than an anomaly; useful as a liquidity control

anomalies.name: amihud liquidity shock / DELTA-illiquidity
anomalies.mechanism: a sudden worsening of a stock's liquidity forecasts near-term underperformance as holders demand compensation or exit
anomalies.counterparty: forced sellers hitting a thinning book
anomalies.known_decay: regime-dependent, strongest in stressed markets

anomalies.name: distance from 52-week low
anomalies.mechanism: stocks far above their 52-week low have positive momentum and less overhang from break-even sellers
anomalies.counterparty: break-even-fixated holders who sell into any recovery near their entry
anomalies.known_decay: overlaps with momentum and dist_52wh feature

anomalies.name: time-series (absolute) momentum
anomalies.mechanism: an asset's own past 12-month excess return predicts its next-month return - slow diffusion of macro information and herding
anomalies.counterparty: investors who rebalance slowly toward a target allocation
anomalies.known_decay: weakened and whipsaw-prone in low-trend regimes post-2010

anomalies.name: moving-average trend rule
anomalies.mechanism: price above a long moving average signals an ongoing uptrend that continues on average; a technical-analysis regularity with a behavioural underreaction story
anomalies.counterparty: slow-to-react investors and stop-loss / trend-following flow
anomalies.evidence: Brock, Lakonishok, LeBaron 1992; Han, Yang, Zhou 2013
anomalies.known_decay: data-mined heavily; robust versions use long windows and cost controls

anomalies.name: residual (idiosyncratic) momentum
anomalies.mechanism: momentum in the part of returns orthogonal to market/size/value is cleaner and less crash-prone than raw momentum
anomalies.counterparty: same underreaction as momentum, with factor-beta noise removed
anomalies.known_decay: holds up better than raw momentum out of sample

anomalies.name: overnight vs intraday return decomposition
anomalies.mechanism: overnight (close-to-open) returns are persistently positive for high-attention retail names while intraday returns mean-revert; the two components carry opposite predictability
anomalies.counterparty: retail order flow concentrated at the open; institutions trade intraday
anomalies.evidence: Lou, Polk, Skouras 2019; Berkman et al. 2012
anomalies.known_decay: documented mostly US; needs careful open-price handling

anomalies.name: avg trade size / order-flow granularity
anomalies.mechanism: volume divided by number of trades proxies for institutional vs retail participation; shifts predict short-horizon returns as informed flow arrives
anomalies.counterparty: uninformed retail splitting into many small trades vs informed institutions in larger clips
anomalies.evidence: Kakushadze 2016 (uses TOTALTRADES-style inputs); microstructure literature on trade-size
anomalies.known_decay: under-studied in EM; genuinely new signal from exchange data

anomalies.name: VWAP deviation / close-vs-vwap
anomalies.mechanism: a close far above the day's VWAP means late-session buying pressure that partly reverts; the gap predicts next-day returns
anomalies.counterparty: end-of-day rebalancers and index flow that must execute near the close
anomalies.evidence: Kakushadze 2016 (multiple alphas use vwap); execution-benchmark literature
anomalies.known_decay: very short-horizon, cost-sensitive

anomalies.name: delivery-percentage momentum (India)
anomalies.mechanism: a high fraction of traded quantity taken to delivery (vs intraday squared off) signals conviction / investment demand rather than speculation, and predicts continuation
anomalies.counterparty: intraday speculators whose flow nets to zero and carries no information about fundamentals
anomalies.evidence: NSE delivery-data studies; India market-microstructure notes
anomalies.known_decay: India-specific; only available from 2019-09-30 in our data

anomalies.name: price-impact (Kyle's lambda) proxy
anomalies.mechanism: the regression slope of return on signed volume measures how much informed trading moves price; stocks with higher lambda command an illiquidity premium
anomalies.counterparty: liquidity providers pricing adverse selection
anomalies.known_decay: estimator-heavy; our version is an Amihud-style approximation

anomalies.name: realized-volatility trend / vol-of-vol
anomalies.mechanism: rising realized volatility forecasts continued elevated volatility and, cross-sectionally, lower risk-adjusted returns for the newly-volatile names
anomalies.counterparty: slow risk-model updaters and investors who do not rebalance for vol
anomalies.known_decay: well known; value is in the cross-section not the level

anomalies.name: downside beta / semi-beta
anomalies.mechanism: stocks that co-move most with the market on down days carry extra risk and a premium; downside beta is priced beyond ordinary beta
anomalies.counterparty: investors who dislike losses asymmetrically (loss aversion)
anomalies.known_decay: small incremental premium; noisy to estimate

anomalies.name: coskewness / skewness preference
anomalies.mechanism: assets that add positive skew to a portfolio are overpriced (investors pay for lottery-like co-movement) and earn lower returns
anomalies.counterparty: investors with a preference for positive skewness
anomalies.known_decay: modest, hard to isolate from IVOL/MAX

anomalies.name: industry momentum
anomalies.mechanism: much of individual-stock momentum is really industry momentum - sector-level information diffuses slowly
anomalies.counterparty: investors slow to rotate across sectors
anomalies.known_decay: still present; our sector labels are coarse (22 NSE industries)

anomalies.name: short-term industry reversal
anomalies.mechanism: within-industry, last week's relative winners revert as sector-level liquidity shocks unwind
anomalies.counterparty: pairs traders and sector rebalancers providing liquidity
anomalies.evidence: Hameed, Huang, Mian 2010; Da, Liu, Schaumburg 2014
anomalies.known_decay: concentrated in the first few days; cost-sensitive

anomalies.name: turn-of-the-month effect
anomalies.mechanism: returns cluster in the last day and first three days of the month - salary/pension inflows and month-end institutional flows
anomalies.counterparty: calendar-driven contributors and index funds investing new cash on a schedule
anomalies.known_decay: still present in aggregate indices; small per-name signal

anomalies.name: same-calendar-month seasonality
anomalies.mechanism: a stock's historical average return in a given calendar month predicts its return in that month again - persistent firm-level seasonalities from recurring information/flows
anomalies.counterparty: investors who ignore recurring calendar patterns in individual names
anomalies.known_decay: replicated internationally; noisy, needs long history

anomalies.name: day-of-week / Monday effect
anomalies.mechanism: average returns differ systematically by weekday - weekend information accumulation and settlement timing
anomalies.counterparty: no clear counterparty; largely an aggregate calendar regularity
anomalies.known_decay: mostly disappeared / reversed since the 1990s - a good negative control

anomalies.name: 52-week-range position (Larson-style)
anomalies.mechanism: where price sits within its trailing 52-week range summarises trend state; mid-range names behave differently from names pinned at an extreme
anomalies.counterparty: range-anchored traders
anomalies.known_decay: overlaps with momentum and dist_52wh

anomalies.name: beta-arbitrage / low-risk within size
anomalies.mechanism: the low-risk premium survives after controlling for size; low-vol small caps are especially mispriced
anomalies.counterparty: benchmark-relative managers who avoid low-beta names for tracking-error reasons
anomalies.known_decay: crowded since ~2012 but not gone

anomalies.name: maximum-drawdown / path-dependence aversion
anomalies.mechanism: stocks with severe recent drawdowns are shunned beyond what fundamentals justify, then partly recover (or the opposite in momentum-crash regimes)
anomalies.counterparty: loss-averse holders who capitulate at the bottom
anomalies.evidence: behavioural finance on realization utility (Barberis & Xiong 2009)
anomalies.known_decay: regime-dependent; sign can flip

anomalies.name: volume-weighted price trend (OBV-style)
anomalies.mechanism: cumulative signed volume (up-days minus down-days) leads price when accumulation is happening quietly
anomalies.counterparty: informed accumulators building a position before news
anomalies.evidence: Granville 1963 (OBV); Blume, Easley, O'Hara 1994 on volume and information
anomalies.known_decay: heavily data-mined; needs cost and look-ahead controls

anomalies.name: size effect
anomalies.mechanism: small-cap stocks have historically earned higher returns than large caps beyond their beta - illiquidity, neglect, and distress risk
anomalies.counterparty: institutions restricted to liquid large caps by mandate
anomalies.known_decay: very weak / absent since the 1980s in raw form; survives mostly interacted with quality

anomalies.name: illiquidity-tail / zero-return days
anomalies.mechanism: the fraction of trading days with (near-)zero returns proxies for latent illiquidity and information dryness; higher counts predict a premium
anomalies.counterparty: holders of thinly-followed names demanding compensation
anomalies.known_decay: useful in EM and small caps; near-zero in liquid names

anomalies.name: pairs / statistical mean-reversion
anomalies.mechanism: co-integrated or historically co-moving stocks whose spread widens tend to converge as relative-value traders step in
anomalies.counterparty: one-sided flow that dislocates a normally-stable spread
anomalies.known_decay: profits declined sharply after ~2002 as the strategy crowded

anomalies.name: seasonal turn-of-year / January small-cap
anomalies.mechanism: tax-loss selling in December depresses small-cap losers, which rebound in January
anomalies.counterparty: tax-motivated sellers acting on the calendar rather than value
anomalies.known_decay: much weaker post-2000; India tax year differs (April) so timing shifts

anomalies.name: post-earnings-announcement drift (PEAD)
anomalies.mechanism: prices underreact to earnings surprises and drift in the direction of the surprise for weeks
anomalies.counterparty: attention-constrained retail and slow institutions
anomalies.known_decay: weakened post-2000 in US large caps; still present in small caps
anomalies.why_not: no earnings dates or estimates in our data

anomalies.name: value / book-to-market
anomalies.mechanism: high book-to-market (cheap) stocks outperform - risk compensation and/or overextrapolation of past growth
anomalies.counterparty: investors extrapolating glamour-stock growth too far
anomalies.known_decay: long drought 2007-2020; strong 2021-2022
anomalies.why_not: no balance-sheet data; size_proxy is not book value

anomalies.name: gross profitability
anomalies.mechanism: firms with high gross profits-to-assets earn higher returns - profitable firms are undervalued relative to their persistence
anomalies.counterparty: investors who focus on earnings and miss gross-margin quality
anomalies.known_decay: robust in research; core of modern quality factors

anomalies.name: asset growth / investment factor
anomalies.mechanism: firms that grow assets aggressively subsequently underperform - overinvestment and market overoptimism
anomalies.counterparty: investors rewarding empire-building management
anomalies.evidence: Cooper, Gulen, Schill 2008; Hou, Xue, Zhang 2015
anomalies.known_decay: one of the more robust fundamental anomalies

anomalies.name: accruals anomaly
anomalies.mechanism: firms with high accruals (earnings not backed by cash flow) have lower future returns - investors fixate on earnings and ignore accrual quality
anomalies.counterparty: investors who take reported earnings at face value
anomalies.known_decay: attenuated after ~2003 once widely published

anomalies.name: net share issuance / buyback
anomalies.mechanism: firms issuing shares underperform; firms buying back outperform - managers time the market and issuance signals overvaluation
anomalies.counterparty: investors who buy secondary offerings at inflated prices
anomalies.known_decay: still present; strong composite with other issuance measures
anomalies.why_not: we deliberately do NOT use shares outstanding (look-ahead trap, P2 step 4c)

anomalies.name: analyst forecast dispersion
anomalies.mechanism: stocks with high disagreement among analysts are overpriced (optimists set the price when shorting is costly) and underperform
anomalies.counterparty: binding-short-constraint means pessimists cannot express their view
anomalies.known_decay: robust; tied to the short-sale-constraint literature

anomalies.name: Piotroski F-score
anomalies.mechanism: a 9-point fundamental-health score separates winners from losers within cheap stocks - the market is slow to price improving fundamentals
anomalies.counterparty: value investors who buy cheap without checking quality
anomalies.known_decay: holds up; widely used in quant value

anomalies.name: dividend yield
anomalies.mechanism: high-dividend-yield stocks have earned higher returns - tax clientele effects and a value tilt
anomalies.counterparty: investors avoiding dividend-payers for tax reasons
anomalies.known_decay: mostly subsumed by value; regime-dependent
anomalies.why_not: corporate-actions feed has ex-dates but not a clean per-share dividend history

anomalies.name: short interest / days-to-cover
anomalies.mechanism: heavily shorted stocks underperform - short sellers are informed, and high short interest signals crowded negative views not yet in price
anomalies.counterparty: retail longs on the other side of informed short flow
anomalies.evidence: Boehmer, Jones, Zhang 2008; Desai et al. 2002
anomalies.known_decay: robust where short data exists
anomalies.why_not: NSE does not publish stock-level short interest in our feed

anomalies.name: credit / distress risk
anomalies.mechanism: financially distressed firms earn LOW returns despite high risk - a puzzle; possibly shareholder expropriation and lottery demand
anomalies.counterparty: investors who gamble on distressed-firm turnarounds
anomalies.known_decay: robust anomaly (negative premium)
anomalies.why_not: no balance-sheet or ratings data - though a price-vol distress proxy is a possible workaround

anomalies.name: media / news sentiment
anomalies.mechanism: negative news-tone predicts short-term underperformance and temporarily higher volume; the market underreacts then reverts
anomalies.counterparty: investors who trade on headline sentiment
anomalies.known_decay: decays fast as text data commoditised

anomalies.name: retail attention (search volume)
anomalies.mechanism: spikes in retail attention (e.g. Google search) precede short-term price run-ups and subsequent reversal
anomalies.counterparty: attention-driven retail buyers
anomalies.known_decay: documented US large caps; noisy elsewhere
anomalies.why_not: no external attention data - our volume/turnover spike is a partial proxy but a different mechanism

anomalies.name: institutional ownership breadth
anomalies.mechanism: a decrease in the number of mutual funds holding a stock (breadth) signals binding short constraints and predicts underperformance
anomalies.counterparty: constrained pessimists who can only 'sell' by not holding
anomalies.known_decay: modest; data-intensive

anomalies.name: option-implied volatility skew
anomalies.mechanism: a steep put-call implied-vol skew signals informed hedging / crash fear and predicts negative returns
anomalies.counterparty: equity holders slow to price what the options market already knows
anomalies.known_decay: robust where liquid single-stock options exist

anomalies.name: earnings announcement premium
anomalies.mechanism: stocks earn abnormally high returns in the days around their scheduled earnings announcement - compensation for announcement risk / attention
anomalies.counterparty: investors who reduce exposure into announcements
anomalies.known_decay: persistent but requires the announcement calendar

anomalies.name: R&D intensity / intangibles
anomalies.mechanism: R&D-intensive firms are undervalued because accounting expenses rather than capitalises R&D, so book value understates the asset base
anomalies.counterparty: investors anchored to reported book value
anomalies.known_decay: part of the modern intangibles-adjusted value discussion
